proposals.before: Zhao Yan, courtesy name Shuq, was from Tianshui.
proposals.after: Zhao Yan, courtesy name Shuqi, was from Tianshui.
proposals.reason: The courtesy name 叔起 should be romanized Shuqi, not truncated Shuq.

proposals.before: Zhao Yan, styled Shuq, was a man of Tianshui.
proposals.after: Zhao Yan, styled Shuqi, was a man of Tianshui.
proposals.reason: The courtesy name 叔起 should be romanized Shuqi, not truncated Shuq.

proposals.before: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, when the capital was moved to Luoyang, Ying and the others were finally able to return home and bury them.
proposals.after: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, Ying and the others were finally able to return home and bury them.
proposals.reason: Chinese and literal English duplicate 遷都洛陽 / the capital-move clause.

proposals.before: Lu and his five brothers are each still young.
proposals.after: We five brothers are each still young.
proposals.reason: Chinese 慮兄弟五人 means five brothers in all (including Lu), not Lu plus five others.

proposals.before: Lu and his five brothers are each still young.
proposals.after: Lu's brothers, five in all, are each still young.
proposals.reason: Chinese 慮兄弟五人 means a total of five brothers including Lu.

decisions.reason: 字叔起 is Shuqi; idiomatic ‘Shuq’ truncates 起 and must be restored to Shuqi.
Same courtesy name 叔起 requires Shuqi in the literal; ‘Shuq’ is a truncation error.
Chapter s0025 dittographs 遷都洛陽; CText Weishu 孝感 reads a single 遷都洛陽 before 子應等乃還鄉葬焉, so collapsing the English capital-move clause is correct.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 年八十卒。遷都洛陽，子應等乃還鄉葬焉。

decisions.reason: 慮兄弟五人 means five brothers including Lu, not Lu plus five; petition voice (s0034–s0037) supports first-person ‘We five brothers’.

decisions.after: Lu and his brothers, five in all, are each still young.
decisions.reason: Before wrongly implies six siblings; the proposed ‘Lu's brothers, five in all’ still reads as five excluding Lu. ‘Lu and his brothers, five in all’ matches 慮兄弟五人.
